newsitem.title: GREECE: GREECE'S PRIORITY SHOULD BE REAL CONVERGENCE - EIB.
newsitem.headline: GREECE'S PRIORITY SHOULD BE REAL CONVERGENCE - EIB.

text.p: Greece's main goal should be the real convergence of its economy with the rest of the European Union since nominal convergence cannot be achieved under the current timetable, said Panayiotis Gennimatas, president of the European Investment Bank (EIB).

"..the main goal should not be the hasty nominal but the real convergence of the Greek economy with the economic system of the European Union that is characterised by more developed production systems and infrastructure," he said speaking at a conference on the Greek economy organised by the American Hellenic Chamber of Commerce.
Greece is the only country in the European Union that does not meet a single convergence criterion as of now.
Its economic and social structure could not sustain an all out effort to attain nominal convergence within the current timetable set by the Maastricht Treaty, he said.

"The political will cannot ignore the stamina of the social base," said Gennimatas who pointed out the weakness of the Greek political system to take and support bold decisions that have political cost.

Nominal convergence should have been the by-product of a strategy to restructure the Greek economy. Implementation should have started in 1981 when Greece was admitted to the European Community or at least in 1992, he said.
"Now, so slowly, so late, we are obliged to seek refuge to tax raids without addressing the real causes that could lead us to a painful restructuring of the economy," said Gennimatas.

Still, Greece had five years to erase its budget deficit, reduce inflation and bring its public debt down but this required a systematic, comprehensive policy on all fronts including foreign policy and national defense, he said.
"We should realise that the EMU is the highest form of national defense for Greece," said Gennimatas. "The common currency will be Greece's spear and shield."
